# Chatbot conversation design — persona, intent mapping, slot filling, error recovery

Curated by Skill Harbor — @seb1n's chatbot-conversation-design skill: a full-lifecycle framework for designing chatbot conversations that survive real users. The agent defines the bot persona and scope first (personality, guardrails, a style guide — a well-scoped bot that nails five tasks beats a vague one attempting fifty), maps intents and entities with journey graphs covering happy paths, branches, and exits, designs slot-filling sequences and disambiguation dialogs (with confirmation prompts for high-stakes actions), builds a three-tier error recovery system (rephrase, constrained options, human escalation — never a dead end), implements context carryover and dialog-state stacks for mid-conversation topic switches, then prototypes, tests, and iterates against metrics like task completion rate and fallback trigger rate. It ships two worked examples (a complete customer-support order-tracking flow and a fallback/escalation flow with state notes), best practices (design the unhappy path first, keep bot utterances under three sentences, confirm irreversible actions, progressive disclosure), and edge-case guidance (multi-intent inputs, topic switching, contradictory info, emotional users, platform constraints like WhatsApp limits). Honest caveats: a design methodology, not a working bot — you still build the bot yourself; the prompt-format template expects you to supply the use case, persona, tasks, and platform. MIT licensed (frontmatter and manifest agree). Skill Harbor...
